ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a D flip-flop with input D on the left, clock input C on the lower left, output Q on the right, and complementary output Q-bar also shown. The output Q is wired back around the top into one input of an AND gate. The other input of the AND gate is A. The output of the AND gate is connected to the D input of the flip-flop. Reasoning: Since the AND gate inputs are A and the feedback value Q, the D input equation is D = A AND Q. Given A = "0", this becomes D = 0 AND Q = 0, regardless of the previous value of Q. When the C pulse arrives, the D flip-flop samples its D input, so the next output Q becomes 0. Therefore, the D flip-flop is set to "0".

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit path: the flip-flop output is looped back through an AND gate to its D input, while A controls that AND gate. With A = 0, the AND gate is disabled, so the line feeding D is forced to logic 0 no matter what the old Q feedback was. When the C pulse arrives, the flip-flop loads this forced-low D value. Thus after the pulse the stored state/output is 0, i.e. the D flip-flop is set to "0".
